segments.title: A page with no backend.
segments.vo: First. A page with no backend.

This page has no server. It is a file on disk. It asked Supabase; Supabase asked SerpApi. Anonymous visitors are refused. Signed-in users get twenty searches a day, each. The key stays in Vault. And every row carries its receipt: replay it from SerpApi's archive for a month, for zero credits.

pg cron calls it every night. Every iPhone on Amazon India, into a table that outlives the sale. Three credits a night. SerpApi as a standing workload, not a tutorial you run once.
A discount is a claim. The ledger is the record. Whichever way the prices move.

segments.subtitle: Installs from a URL  ·  Supabase hosted  ·  Supabase local  ·  Postgres 17
segments.vo: Under the hood: one Rust wrapper, compiled to Wasm, installed from a URL. It fails closed at the cap, before the HTTP call, and never prints the key in an error.
The same search as Markdown, straight from the database. An agent's SQL tool reads a page instead of parsing JSON.
